title: Exact Power of Two
statement:
Given a 32-bit signed integer n, return true if n equals 2k for some whole number k ≥ 0, and false otherwise.

Note that 1 = 20 counts, while zero and negative numbers never do. Try to answer without a loop.

examples.why: 64 = 2⁶. In binary it is 1000000: a single 1 bit.
2⁰ = 1. A loop that starts by dividing by 2 tends to get this one wrong.
No power of two is negative, even though 8 is one.

hints: Write a few powers of two in binary. What do they all have in common?
A positive power of two has exactly one 1 bit. How can you clear the lowest 1 bit of a number?
n & (n − 1) removes the lowest set bit. For a positive n, the result is 0 exactly when that bit was the only one.

explain.intuition:
In binary, powers of two look like 1, 10, 100, 1000: one single 1 bit. So the question becomes "is n positive with exactly one bit set?"

Subtracting 1 flips the lowest 1 bit to 0 and every 0 below it to 1, for example 1000 − 1 = 0111. ANDing that with n wipes out the lowest 1 bit and leaves the rest. If nothing remains, there was only one bit. The n > 0 check handles 0 and negatives, whose two's complement form can have one bit set too (-2³¹ is 1000…0).
pitfalls: Forgetting n > 0. Zero passes the bit test (0 & -1 = 0), and so does -2³¹.
Using floating-point Math.log2(n) and checking for a whole number. Rounding errors make that fragile for large inputs.
Operator precedence in C-like languages: n & n - 1 == 0 parses as n & ((n - 1) == 0). Use parentheses.

solutions.title: Divide by two while even
solutions.idea: Keep halving while the number is even. A power of two ends at exactly 1.

solutions.title: Clear the lowest set bit
solutions.idea: A positive power of two has a single 1 bit, so removing the lowest 1 bit with n & (n − 1) leaves zero.
